Implementing this model effectively comes with several challenges. First, ensuring accurate identification of students who need support without unnecessary intrusions into their privacy is critical. This requires careful balancing of data usage and continual evaluation to avoid false positives or negatives.

Another challenge is resource allocation—having enough staff trained in effective outreach strategies will be essential for making this system work well. Advisors would need time and resources to build trusting relationships through personalised support, which can't happen if we're stretched too thin managing administrative tasks.

Additionally, there's the risk of creating a sense of surveillance among students if not handled properly. Clear communication about how data is being used and why will be crucial for maintaining trust in this process.

Finally, adapting to different student needs across diverse groups means designing interventions that are flexible enough to address individual circumstances while still providing structured support when needed most.
